kamokya-drain-a.title: File:Drainage channel in Kamokya, Kampala (4331539359).jpg
kamokya-drain-a.author: SuSanA Secretariat
kamokya-drain-a.description:
When contaminated with human excreta the drainages pose a significant risk of spreading diseases. A common emptying practice for the pit latrines is to open the pits when it is raining heavily. Thus the pit latrines get emptyied for "free". The remains of that process often stay in the drainages. Two recent outbreaks of cholera in another slum area witness that risk. 
Photo: Enno Schröder, Uganda

kamokya-drain-b.title: File:Drainage channel, solid waste heap and footpath in Kamokya, Kampala (4331538683).jpg
kamokya-drain-b.author: SuSanA Secretariat
kamokya-drain-b.description:
Due to a lack of planning, bottle necks like this occur quite often (The path continues to the right after passing the house in front). They create problems regarding the transportation of urine or faeces from the UDDTs. Especially after a rain this path almost becomes impassable.
Photo: Enno Schröder, Uganda 2010

natete-drain.title: File:Drainage channel in Natete, Kampala (4332278352).jpg
natete-drain.author: SuSanA Secretariat
natete-drain.description:
Especially after heavy rainfalls or when blocked by rubbish, the water in the channels becomes stagnant.
Photo: Enno Schröder, Uganda 2009

kalerwe-drain.title: File:Garbage disposal in drainage channel along Kalerwe-Bwaise road, Kampala.jpg
kalerwe-drain.author: MEvalyn
kalerwe-drain.description: With the wastes poorly disposed off in the drainage channel it increases the rate of the chemical reactions which leads to various products especially the green house gases. These gases rise and get trapped in the atmosphere resulting in warm air, rise in environmental temperatures and in the long run may result in to drought.
